floor_layers._pick: E3 L1 hall planks: position-hashed variants from the light plank swatch
E3 L1 kitchen zone: grey cobble swatch
E3 L1 bedroom corner: herringbone swatch

entities.observe: A young human, no armor, no weapon, no idea she is the strangest thing in this world. She moves like someone still deciding to be brave. The inn already leans toward her.
entities.friendly_line: Oh - hi! You've got a good face, you know that? Come in, sit down. I'll find you something warm - on the house, probably. Don't tell Lyonette I said that.
talk_pool: Oh! Hi. Sorry - I was somewhere else in my head. You need something? I can usually find something.
Welcome to The Wandering Inn! That's the whole speech. I'm still workshopping the rest of it.
Everything okay? You've got a look. I know that look - I make that look in mirrors.
If you hear yelling about a door later, that's just the inn being the inn. Don't worry about it.

lines: Hey, you! Good timing. I just invented a new way to burn soup. Kidding. Mostly. Sit, sit.
You know you don't have to hover by the door anymore, right? You're basically furniture now. Nice furniture.
Selys asked about you the other day. I said nice things. You owe me one truthful compliment about my pasta.
There you are! Sit down, I'm testing a recipe on you. That came out wrong. WITH you. Testing it with you.
Lyonette hums when she scrubs now. She'd deny it under oath, so don't tell her I said anything. That was you, by the way.
Some days this place is a lot. Then somebody walks in and it's less a lot. You're one of the less-a-lot ones.

talk_pool_stages._comment: CONSTRAINT: this stage deliberately repeats every waking until the residue stage below takes over; it is the game's only signpost toward the new door, so it must keep firing until the player has actually acted on it, never for a fixed number of hearings.
lines: You didn't say anything, so I will: there's a door in the inn that wasn't there yesterday. It's mine. It's — new. Go look, if you want. Just... knock first. Old habit.

talk_pool_stages._comment: Array-order-wins: authored last, wins the moment the gate is met.
lines: Still there this morning. I checked before breakfast. Okay, during. I checked during breakfast.
Take whoever needs it in there sometime. That's what it's for. I think that's what it's for.

dialogue.speaker: Erin
dialogue.text: Welcome to The Wandering Inn! Mind giving that table a wipe?

entities.observe: A human girl playing at composure a size too large for her. Her hands know trays; her chin knows courts. The two have not finished arguing.
entities.friendly_line: Lyonette's chin lifts, then softens despite itself. You're kind. People are not, usually, to the help. ...It is a small thing. It is not nothing. Sit where you like; I'll bring something hot.
talk_pool: Yes, I work here. No, I did not always. That is the whole story, and you may have it for the price of a nod.
The floors are clean because I cleaned them. Twice. Mind where you set your boots.
...You said thank you. To me. Hm. Most don't. — Well. Don't let it go to your head.

lines: You covered for me. With the order, I mean. You didn't have to, and you didn't make it a story to tell later. That is... rare. Thank you.
Sit anywhere you like. The good chair by the fire, even. No, I insist — I'm allowed to insist, it's practically my inn too.
I used to think kindness was something people spent on you to get something back. You keep not doing that. It's unsettling. In a good way. Mostly.

dialogue.speaker: Lyonette
dialogue.text: Mind the floors, they're just done.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The table's a mess of rings and crumbs. It wants a proper wipe-down.

entities._comment: Kept as pure flavor: banks read_dusty_scroll (referenced nowhere as a gate) and toasts a hint that magic exists and is learnable from someone who knows it.
entities.toast: Faded arcane script. You can't read a word of it. Whoever penned this knew magic you don't. Someone in the city must.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The wick's dry and ready. All it wants is a light that doesn't need a match.

on_skill_use.toast: [Light] — A steady white orb settles into the lantern's glass.

entities._comment: Never a quest-giver/vendor (the Serve mini-loop is a repeatable chore, not a quest)

entities.once_per_waking_toast: The tables are covered. Nothing more to carry out until tomorrow.
entities.toast: You carry the laden tray out to the tables.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The kettle's on. The inn won't mind one more thing brewing, so long as it means well.
entities.locked_toast: A kettle, singing low. It's just a kettle, unless you know otherwise.

on_skill_use.toast: [Hedge Remedy] — The inn's kettle does in a pinch, just like she said. The steam settles into something kinder.

entities.skill_hint_toast: Good stock, better knives, and nobody using either. A real cook could turn this counter into a meal worth naming.
entities.locked_toast: A working counter, scrubbed and stocked. The kitchen has standards, and they're looking at you.

on_skill_use.toast: [Advanced Cooking] — Knife-work first, then the pan, then the part nobody can teach. The plate comes out arguing for seconds.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The good copper pan. It's been waiting for a dish that deserves it.
entities.locked_toast: The good copper pan, hung out of easy reach. Erin's rule, probably.

on_skill_use.toast: [Signature Dish] — The pan remembers you now. What comes out of it isn't dinner, it's a reputation.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The stew's at the turn. Someone who knows a pot could bring it home.
entities.locked_toast: You don't know your way around a stew pot. Yet.

on_skill_use.toast: [Basic Cooking] — The stew comes out rich and hot.

entities.skill_hint_toast: Three plates, one order, no sense. Someone who can cook could untangle it.
entities.locked_toast: The order's a mess and you haven't the first idea how to stretch it. Not yet.

on_skill_use.toast: [Basic Cooking] — You thin the stock, fold in day-old bread, and stretch the short order into a full service. Lyonette's shortfall vanishes into the pot.

entities.observe: A plain plank door, warped at the bottom from a hundred winters. Nothing about it looks like it goes anywhere but the pantry.
entities._comment_d4: portal_menu_when is checked before the fallback interaction; once door_awakened is met, the picker replaces the flavor toast.
entities.toast: Onions, a sack of soft potatoes, a shelf of jarred somethings gone dusty. The pantry door, same as it's always been.

visual_states._comment: No `sprite` key here now: it stays the plain pantry door, only the cool-blue tint (the flicker tell) applied.

entities._comment: `allies:["relc"]`/`ally_requires:{met_relc:1}` mirrors D2's own harness gated cell (`rift_vermin_leak_w8_relc`, the 0.55-0.95 tuned band) rather than the harder ungated `_solo` variant.
entities.observe: A hairline crack seams the plaster here, and the draft through it is colder than a pantry has any right to be. Something small moves on the other side of it, and doesn't like being watched back.

entities._comment: the field-skill first-use idiom (cellar_door/nest_ledge precedent), `requires_skill: observe` (the Tactician L1 grant, matching nest_ledge/cisterns_scout) + `on_skill_use` banks `read_the_door_runes` (an intermediate counter, zero rng) deterministically.
entities.skill_hint_toast: The grain of the frame almost makes a pattern, if the right eye looked at it properly.

on_skill_use.toast: [Observe] — The grain of the frame isn't grain at all: a pattern worked into the wood, old and deliberate, repeating around the jamb like a held breath. It doesn't move while you watch it. It moves the instant you look away.

entities.locked_toast: The doorframe's old wood is carved with something under the paint, faint and worn. Whatever it says isn't for an untrained eye.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The old marks under the paint are almost gone. Almost.
entities.locked_toast: Scratches under the doorframe paint. Could be anything. Could be nothing.

on_skill_use.toast: [Detect Magic] — The old wardwork wakes just enough to be read: someone bound this cellar's door long before it learned to go elsewhere.

entities._comment: CONSTRAINT: the free approach cell is (3,7), facing down (same column as before, shifted onto the wall).
entities.observe: Plaster, old and thin, and a nail with nothing hung on it. If something is meant to be here, it isn't yet.
entities.toast: Bare wall. A nail with nothing hung on it.

door_when.open_toast: The vines part like a curtain, and the light beyond doesn't flicker.

entities._comment: talk_pool + a static dialogue fallback (no conversation graph, the Renn/Ilvo/Yelra pool-presence idiom).
talk_pool: The couch by the fire is Yvlon's now. Territorial, armswomen.
Pisces keeps asking about the vault door. I told him to bring his own rope this time.
Silver-rank pay, Gold-rank stonework down there. Somebody's math is off, and it isn't mine.

lines: I trained formal, once. Robes, theory, the whole overpriced show. Doesn't come up much anymore, and I like it that way.
You want a tip that's actually useful? Watch the ice before you stand on it. I learned that one the expensive way.
Yvlon says I've gone soft since the inn. I say I've gone SMART. There's a difference, and it involves not getting frostbite on purpose anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Ceria Springwalker
dialogue.text: Ask me about the vault again and I'll start charging Pisces rent.

talk_pool: The inn's quieter than the Guild hall. I'm starting to see why you like it.
If the door down there opens, I want to be standing in front of it. That's not bravery — it's just where I stand.

lines: Ask about the arms all you like, now. Silver-steel, shapeable, better grip than flesh ever gave me. I've stopped flinching from the question, so you don't have to either.
Keep your guard up on your off-hand side. Most people forget it exists until something reminds them, and I'd rather you learn it from me than the hard way.
The couch by the fire really is mine. Ceria just likes saying otherwise.

talk_pool: I have been given a mug of blue fruit juice. I did not ask for it. Erin says this is called 'hospitality.' I am recording it as an asset.
This inn does not have traps. I checked all the floors. Twice.
Captain Ceria says I may sit anywhere. I have chosen the corner with two exits.

lines: I was Prognugator, once. Command caste. I was exiled, is the word Klbkch uses. 'Reassigned' is the word I prefer. Neither changes what happened.
I have counted every safe path between here and the pantry door. If you ever need the fastest one, comrade, ask. I keep the count current.
Erin gave me a name for the corner I sit in. She calls it 'Ksmvr's Post.' I have accepted the designation. It is efficient.

dialogue.speaker: Ksmvr
dialogue.text: I am still counting exits. There are still two.
